zones.label: Beginner Track
facts: First Scratch sprite and block-coding projects
Heavy use of unplugged coding activities to build vocabulary before screens
Success measured by finishing and sharing one complete project

zones.label: Intermediate Track
zones.summary: The block-to-text transition and core Python.
facts: Python variables, loops, and conditionals introduced one at a time
Turtle graphics challenges provide visual verification
Peer code review starts here, as students have enough code to review

zones.label: Advanced Track
facts: Combines functions, loops, and conditionals into a single project like a simple game
Pair programming and live coding demonstrations become regular practice
Students often begin serving as peer mentors (Chapter 9) themselves
Strongest fit for professional mentor involvement

quiz.question: Which track introduces Python variables and loops one at a time?
Which track uses unplugged activities to build vocabulary before screens?
In which track do students often start peer mentoring?
